messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@acme-retail.com>

Cc: 
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rehydration & rerank — scope/questions before kickoff

Hi Camila / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to formalize the migration for our search embeddings and the rerank evaluation so we can move to Redwood-managed scoring in production. Before the kickoff, a few things we want to confirm so we can align internal stakeholders: 

- Current footprint: ~2.4M product text embeddings (768-dim) stored in an older Pinecone cluster. Primary index is per-region (US/EU) with soft-fallover to global.
- Goal: backfill a new Weaviate cluster (managed by our infra) but served through Redwood routing for scoring. We want to keep the existing product IDs unchanged.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th percentile query latency < 220ms (US), rerank MAP uplift >= 6% on our 4K test queries, and under 15% of queries flagged for manual review due to relevance drift.

Questions: 
1) What does Redwood need from us to run parallel rerank evals (sample format, labeling expectations)?
2) Any recommended phasing for backfill to avoid search regressions? Can we run a hybrid read-fallback while seeding?
3) Do you recommend any quantization or float->int steps for the vector store we should plan with infra?

We'll need a short mutual action plan and an initial working session this week if possible — Priya and I are available Wed/Thu mornings PT.

Attached: a short export of our index stats and a small labeled set (rerank-eval-sample.jsonl) so you can sanity-check sample size.

Thanks,
Alex Porter
Senior Product Manager, Search
Acme Retail
[Attachment: index-stats-20270325.csv (text/csv)]

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@acme-retail.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Retail — index rehydration plan & rerank evaluation scope

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the samples. Looping in Jordan (on operations) and Grace (CS/QA) to cover rollout and eval gating.

High level answers up front:
- What we need: a JSONL sample with query, candidate_ids, gold_rank (or relevance label), and the original embedding for at least 4k queries for a robust rerank run. Your sample is a good start; we'll ask for a stratified sample across categories (new products, retired SKUs, high-frequency queries).
- Phasing recommendation: three waves — (1) pilot wave (1% traffic to Redwood scoring with the new index, blue-green reads), (2) staged backfill with region-level cutovers and prefetched KV caching for hot prefixes, (3) full cutover with automated fallback policy to the old index for regressions. Hybrid read-fallback is supported and recommended during Wave 2.
- Vector store considerations: avoid lossy quantization during initial backfill. If you need int8 later for cost, we recommend running quantized variants as shadow indices during evaluation and shipping quantization recommendations in Redwood Optimize after acceptance.

I've attached a short outline (ACME_index-rehydrate-outline.xlsx) that maps owners, decision points, and a suggested 6-week timeline. Proposed working session: Thu, Apr 1, 9:30–10:30am PT — will that work for you and Priya?

Next steps I propose (owners):
- Acme: share stratified 4k eval set and a list of top 500 hot product IDs (Alex) — due Tue EOD PT.
- Redwood: run initial rerank smoke (Jordan) and share baseline metrics + recommended thresholds (Grace) — deliver by Fri.
- Joint: 1-hr kickoff working session to agree M.A.P. and escalation path.

A few risk notes: watch for ID collisions if product IDs have prefixes; keep a mapping table if you plan to change canonical IDs during migration. Also plan for query-level sampling so we can detect cold-start regressions for long-tail queries.

I'll add the invite once you confirm the Thu slot.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Dropping in a short ops checklist so the team can see concrete tasks and owners before the kickoff. Camila — feel free to edit.

Execution runbook (high level):
- Prep stage (Acme): export stratified eval JSONL (4k queries) + top-500 hot IDs, export current Pinecone mapping table (Alex) — DUE: Tue 2027-03-30 17:00 PT.
- Smoke run (Redwood): ingest sample into a staging Weaviate index (shadow) and run rerank scoring against your current ranker -> produce delta metrics (Jordan).
- Pilot traffic routing (Redwood+Acme): configure 1% traffic via Redwood routing to new index; enable read-fallback to Pinecone for mismatches. Monitor top-queries latency and QPS tails.
- Backfill plan: chunked job by product category with checksum verification and ID mapping audits. Use backoff windows during heavy traffic periods.
- Eval gating: Grace to define gating thresholds (MAP uplift, NDCG improvements, and false-positive review rate). If any gate fails, auto-failover to previous scoring variant for affected query buckets.

I'll attach a small runbook note with CLI commands and expected monitoring panels for our console.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
On-call Operations, Redwood Inference
